node.title: Calcium signalling and mitochondrial ATP production
node.canonical_question: How does calcium signalling inside mitochondria affect ATP production?
node.summary: Calcium ions enter the matrix via the MCU and activate Krebs cycle dehydrogenases. This raises NADH and FADH2 supply to the electron transport chain, increasing ATP output.

core.explanation: Calcium ions (Ca2+) reach the mitochondrial matrix through a protein channel called the mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU). Once inside, elevated Ca2+ activates three enzymes of the Krebs cycle: pyruvate dehydrogenase (via a Ca2+-activated phosphatase), isocitrate dehydrogenase, and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase. Activating these enzymes increases the rate at which acetyl-CoA is oxidised, generating more NADH and FADH2 per unit time. These electron carriers donate more electrons to the electron transport chain, which pumps more protons across the inner membrane, steepens the proton gradient, and drives ATP synthase faster. Some evidence also suggests Ca2+ can stimulate ATP synthase directly. The overall result is that a rise in mitochondrial Ca2+ acts as a demand signal: when cytoplasmic Ca2+ rises during events such as muscle contraction or intense neuronal firing, mitochondria sense this and upregulate ATP production to meet the increased energy demand.
key_points: Ca2+ enters the mitochondrial matrix through the mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU).
Elevated matrix Ca2+ activates pyruvate dehydrogenase, isocitrate dehydrogenase, and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.
Greater dehydrogenase activity increases NADH and FADH2 production from the Krebs cycle.
More electron carriers supply the electron transport chain, increasing proton pumping and ATP synthesis.
Calcium therefore couples cytoplasmic demand signals to mitochondrial ATP output.

rendering.summary: Calcium ions flood into the mitochondria when a cell is very active. Inside, they switch on enzymes that make more NADH and FADH2, giving the electron transport chain more fuel so ATP synthase spins faster and produces more ATP.
rendering.analogy: Think of calcium as a message from the factory floor saying demand is high. When the message arrives, the supply team in the mitochondria speeds up production to keep up.
